findings.reason: The original standalone tiles correctly render the formula but do not expose its two composable paths. A fixed-psi square materially clarifies the R(G)-module compatibility of induction: restriction enters the H-ring multiplication, whereas multiplication after induction takes place in R(G). This is a warranted explanatory addition under the expanded diagram scope, not a claim that absence alone is a parser failure.

diagram_math_checks.result: Upper row is R(H), lower row R(G). Both vertical maps are Ind_H^G:R(H)->R(G), defined on ordinary characters by the local induced-character definition and extended additively to virtual characters by F4/step 3.1. Restriction sends a G-character to its H-character (same underlying representation with H action); hence Res_H^G psi lies in R(H).

For fixed psi in R(G), upper map chi |-> chi Res_H^G psi maps R(H) to R(H), and lower map eta |-> eta psi maps R(G) to R(G). Ring closure and bilinearity are in def-virtual-character-and-character-ring-of-a-finite-group and F4. Each map is additive. For ordinary characters, F2 and thm-characters-of-direct-sums-tensor-products-and-duals identify these products with tensor products of two H-representations or two G-representations respectively.

All arrows point right or down. Top then right yields Ind_H^G(chi Res_H^G psi); left then bottom yields (Ind_H^G chi) psi, both in R(G). These are equal by steps 1.1-2.1 for honest characters and step 3.1 for virtual characters. No inverse relation between induction and restriction, nor categorical tensor-functor identity, is asserted.

Restriction preserves products because restricted tensor-product actions are the same H-actions; together with pointwise addition, this gives the stated R(G)-action psi dot chi=(Res psi)chi. The square expresses exactly its compatibility with induction. Original steps 1.1-4.1 are byte-identical and do not use the figure.
